item.title: Chichibu Night Festival: One of Japan's Three Great Float Festivals — Guide
item.description: The Chichibu Night Festival, held each December, is ranked among Japan’s three great float festivals and designated a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. Six enormous, elaborately decorated floats — some weighing several tonnes and adorned with intricate wood carvings, lanterns and tapestries — are hauled through the streets by teams of local residents, accompanied by traditional flute and drum music, while a spectacular fireworks display lights the winter sky above. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Chichibu, Saitama Hours Evening, December 2–3 each year Admission Free to view Time needed 3–5 hours (evening parade + fireworks) Best time December 3 evening (main event) What to See Six enormous decorated floats, some weighing several tonnes.

item.title: Hakodate Christmas Fantasy Guide: Dates, Lights & Access
item.description: Each December, Hakodate’s romantic bayfront glows for Hakodate Christmas Fantasy — a festive waterfront event built around a giant illuminated Christmas tree floating in the harbour. Set against the historic Kanemori Red Brick Warehouses and reflected in the water, the tree (a gift tradition linked to sister-city Halifax) is joined by sparkling illuminations, a nightly light-up “moment,” soup kitchens with hot food, and even fireworks. Combined with Hakodate’s world-famous night view from the mountain, it makes the city a magical place to be in early winter.

item.title: Naha Marathon Guide: Date, Course & Entry
item.description: The Naha Marathon is one of Japan’s most popular and warmly welcoming road races — a full marathon held each December under Okinawa’s mild winter skies. Tens of thousands of runners loop from central Naha through the southern part of the island, cheered on by legendary local support: residents line the route handing out snacks, awamori and high-fives in true Okinawan style. With a sub-tropical climate and festive atmosphere, it’s a bucket-list race for runners and a fun spectacle for visitors.

item.title: Tokyo Winter Illuminations Guide December 2026
item.description: Tokyo in December: The Ultimate Guide to Winter Illuminations, Christmas Markets & Seasonal Food There is something almost magical about Tokyo in December. The air turns crisp, the ginkgo trees shed their last golden leaves, and suddenly—almost overnight—the entire city transforms into a shimmering wonderland of light. If you have never experienced Tokyo in December winter illuminations Christmas season, you are missing one of the most visually stunning urban spectacles on the planet.

item.title: Tokyo Winter Illuminations Guide December 2026 Best Spots
item.description: Tokyo Winter Illuminations Guide December Best Spots: A Local’s Complete Seasonal Handbook There’s a moment every late November when Tokyo transforms. The last amber ginkgo leaves are still clinging to their branches, but the city has already begun wrapping itself in millions of tiny lights. If you’ve never experienced a Tokyo December, you’re missing one of the most visually spectacular — and underrated — seasons to visit Japan’s capital. This Tokyo winter illuminations guide December best spots roundup is something I update every year after personally walking every major display, and I’m convinced that winter Tokyo rivals any Christmas market in Europe for pure atmosphere.
